entries.test: Published match records and reporting would establish Pelrine's amateur status, the AI opponent's strength, and the 14–1 result.
Public studies from the seven years preceding publication would show whether deep learning repeatedly produced unexpected failures and behavior unlike humans on comparable tasks.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives 'unpredictable' a plain reading in terms of unexpected adversarial failures.

entries.test: Published adversarial evaluations comparing human and deep learning performance would establish whether repeated attacks exposed substantial model weaknesses absent in humans.
entries.note: In context, the comparison concerns behavior and vulnerabilities.

entries.test: Public research accounts and match records would establish whether Pelrine learned Gleave's adversarial strategy and repeatedly won using it.
entries.note: Whether the earlier research and the reported match used the same strategy is part of the test.
'Never be sure' supplies no shared standard of certainty or specified range of novel circumstances. Individual generalization failures cannot settle that unrestricted assertion.

entries.test: Public technical analyses of driverless-car setbacks and chatbot errors from the week before publication would show whether failures to generalize contributed to both.
entries.note: The proposition attributes the failures to a common underlying problem, making it causal.
The terminology about network layers is checkable, but 'conceptual depth' has no shared operational meaning that would settle the full claim.
